primary_claim: A tiny 1-layer ReLU network trained to output sparse top-k distributions over a vocabulary much larger than its residual dimension learns a mechanism closely resembling a Bloom filter (sparse binary token hashes, hidden-layer union indicator, output logits read from set intersection), achieving 0.031 total variation distance on held-out samples, with error scaling like O(log(1/delta)) in width versus polynomial scaling for a standard superposition (JL-style) solution.

effect.metric: total variation distance to target top-k distribution; false positive rate
effect.value: 0.031 TVD on held-out random samples; ~2.4% (2438/100000) of random token sets produced a Bloom-filter-style false positive under the TVD-based detection threshold (<0.95 top-k mass)

depends_on: The Softmax Bottleneck Does Not Limit the Probabilities of the Most Likely Tokens (OpenReview)
contradicts_or_qualifies: standard JL-style superposition accounts of how networks represent more features than dimensions, which the author argues would need width scaling polynomially in 1/delta rather than logarithmically
stated_future_work: fully understand/prove the mechanism behind the 1-layer model, ideally with a rigorous proof rather than mechanistic evidence
determine the scaling for the density of hashes the model learns and relate it to theoretical Bloom filter density
investigate what mechanisms real LLMs learn to output sparse distributions over vocabularies comparable in size to d_model
limitations_stated: this is just a toy network, so it doesn't directly tell us what larger models do
the mechanistic analysis is incomplete: it can explain why false positives are rare but not precisely why the model gets so close to a uniform distribution over top-k tokens
the exact construction has not been rigorously proven to hold for the trained network, only supported by mechanistic evidence
quote: The trained network seems to converge to a mechanism closely resembling a Bloom filter: tokens are assigned sparse binary hashes, the hidden layer computes an approximate union indicator, and the output logits are linearly read from this union.
